messages.author: e8ad54d4ad5b752c
messages.subject: count()
parts:
When using this function is there a way to fill in 0's for empty combinations?

For example, the dataframe below I would like a 0 for 1995, 1997-1999, 2001-2002
1994 2
1996 1
2000 1
2003 1

messages.author: d5bd2ee38320ab47
messages.subject: Re: count()
parts:
Yes you can try :
t0 <- c(1995, 1997:1999, 2001:2002)
x0 <- rep(0, length(t0))

t1 <- c(1994, 1996, 2000, 2003)
x1 <- c(2, 1, 1, 1)

t <- c(t0, t1)
x<-c(x0,x1)

df <- data.frame(t, x)

df <- df[order(t),]



... but it is likely there is an easiest solution !

Yours, Nicolas Vaillant

messages.author: 657fe4fd7514e3f5
messages.subject: Re: count()
parts:
Hi Rachel,

One way would be to coerce your years into a factor so that the uncounted years be recognized as a level. Or, if it's already a factor, skip immediately to line 5 of the code.

x <- c(1994,1994,1996,2000,2003)
yrs <- 1994:2003

xf <- factor(x, labels = yrs, levels = yrs)
xcounts <- as.data.frame(table(xf))

Hope that helps.

Best,
Sean

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: count()
parts:
The single line of Description for plyr::count() (which I assume you
mean as opposed to dplyr::count(), version 0.3+) states:

"Equivalent to as.data.frame(table(x)), but does not include
combinations with zero counts."

Therefore, if you want to include years with zero counts, coerce year
to a factor and apply the table() function to it.

Reproducible example:

year <- factor(sample(1995:2010, 15, replace = TRUE), levels = 1995:2010)
as.data.frame(table(year))

BTW, this is not a ggplot2-related question. It belongs on R-help or
StackOverflow (R tag).

Dennis
